revision_note: 2026-09-21 (fixed generation templates, user-approved optimization): production no longer searches for a usable size through progressively smaller prompts. A brief locks one macro-pixel template before generation; retries keep the same canvas, subject zone, centre axis and contact baseline. Humanoids use 32x64; horizontal beasts and other non-humanoid units preselect the smallest fitting 32-multiple canvas, capped at 64x64 for ordinary single-cell units. Decoding verifies the locked template and never resizes. Prior note: 2026-09-21 (asset semantics and scene assembly): runtime art roles are declared before generation and may not combine walkable ground with blocking walls. Concept room shells are review references only. New manifests record placement semantics, mount type, visible contact line, depth baseline, support object and screen axis. Scene batches lock a shared material palette family and fixed upper-left form light before generation; assembly review checks gameplay semantics before aesthetics. Ground tiles keep the current baked material-dark 1 px border and inner lip. Prior note: 2026-09-21 (indoor real scale): ordinary indoor objects use common real-world dimensions at 1 native px = 3.125 cm. Prior note: 2026-09-21 (stage art direction): the current academy stage is Japanese fantasy magic isekai while aether remains measurable engineering. Prior note: 2026-09-16 (ground tiles): the battlefield uses one 32x32 ground square per gameplay cell on one 32 PPU grid.

small_prop_scale_rule.principle: PPU is a project-wide constant, never a per-asset choice. Changing it per object would put two different pixel sizes on the same battlefield, which is exactly the defect the display policy exists to prevent.
small_prop_scale_rule.true_scale_reference: at 1 px = 3.125 cm: 100 cm = 32 px, 50 cm = 16 px, 40 cm = 13 px, 30 cm = 10 px, 20 cm = 6 px, 10 cm = 3 px
small_prop_scale_rule.how_to_make_a_small_object: keep 32 PPU and shrink the drawing inside the 32x32 cell canvas, bottom-centre anchored to the owning cell. The existing material_pickup_24_to_ui32 role already does exactly this: a 24x24 subject embedded unscaled at offset (4,4) inside a 32x32 canvas.
small_prop_scale_rule.answer_to_do_we_need_16_ppu: no. A sub-50 cm prop does not need a smaller PPU; it needs a smaller drawing or a smaller subject canvas inside the same 32 PPU grid. 16 PPU is a retired experiment and must not be reintroduced.
small_prop_scale_rule.readability_floor: below about 40 cm the true-scale drawing is 12 px or less and reads as a coloured blob rather than an identifiable object. Those props are drawn at roughly 1.5x to 2x true scale so the player can tell what they are, and the deliberate over-scale is recorded in the manifest.
never: change the project PPU per asset
resample or halve an existing asset to fit a small object
introduce a second pixel size on the battlefield

world_scale.anchor: one native pixel = 3.125 cm; one gameplay cell = 32x32 native px = 1.00 m square
world_scale.why_this_value: the character spec (body 46-58 px) was locked independently for the silhouette, and only at a 1 m cell does it land inside the human height range (1.44-1.81 m). A 1.25 m cell would make every humanoid 1.80-2.27 m and a 1.5 m cell 2.16-2.72 m, which is visibly giant. The two decisions therefore confirm each other, and every later size question can be derived from this single number instead of re-negotiating PPU or display scale.
world_scale.vertical_caveat: side-view characters are drawn at true metric height, so their pixel height is a real height. Top-down ground and walls are a projection: their canvas height is a height cue, not a measured height. Indestructible terrain fills its cell and is defined to block movement and sight lines regardless of how tall its sprite looks.

indoor_real_scale_policy.principle: ordinary indoor objects use common real-world dimensions instead of per-image aesthetic scaling

battlefield_placement_rules.R1: gameplay cell = 32x32 native px; exactly one 32x32 ground tile per cell, no subgrid and no cross-cell base texture
battlefield_placement_rules.R2: objects anchor bottom-center to the owning cell's bottom edge; multi-cell objects use the bottom-left cell as the owning cell, bottom edge on the footprint's lowest row and horizontal center on the footprint center
battlefield_placement_rules.R3: overhang above, left and right is allowed; overhang past the footprint's bottom edge toward the screen bottom is forbidden, except for the ground front face which is defined to overhang its own cell southward by 8 px
battlefield_placement_rules.R4: layer order back to front: ground, ground front faces, ground overlays, walls, large structures, small props, units, overlays
battlefield_placement_rules.R5: within a layer sort by bottom-edge y ascending, then by category priority structure < prop < unit
battlefield_placement_rules.R6: humanoid units keep a 32x64 canvas; non-humanoid units preselect the smallest fitting 32-multiple canvas up to 64x64; all keep the body on the declared contact baseline without runtime resizing
battlefield_placement_rules.R7: a ground front face is drawn after the next row's ground and before any wall, structure, prop or unit in that row, so the raised block occludes the cell in front of it while units still draw over both
battlefield_placement_rules.R8: new assets declare mount type and visible contact line before generation; depth sorting uses that contact line rather than transparent canvas bounds
battlefield_placement_rules.R9: floor-standing, wall-mounted and tabletop variants are distinct application roles; changing only scene coordinates never changes an asset's mount type
battlefield_placement_rules.R10: a runtime room separates walkable 32x32 ground, blocking 32x32 walls, directional edges or front faces, and independent props; a combined room shell is concept-only
battlefield_placement_rules.R11: runtime layout review verifies walkability, collision, click ownership and occlusion before visual polish
battlefield_placement_rules.R12: every scene assembly records native coordinates and draw order and is reviewed at native 1x and canonical 6x

attack_range_presentation.committable_target: committed tier; requires an alive non-hero unit on the cell and no global failure
attack_range_presentation.dead_zone: closer than the weapon's own minimum range; uses the unreachable texture at the unavailable tier instead of being left blank
attack_range_presentation.review: EditMode tier, ladder-ordering, eligibility and dead-zone tests pass; steady-state rendered alpha read back 0.44 movement and attack envelope, 0.27 spell reach envelope, 0.44 skill selectable anchor; human aesthetic review pending

spell_reach_presentation.source: FireSpellEngine.Preview failures, so the reach field and the resolver share one geometry instead of restating distance and line-of-sight here
spell_reach_presentation.applies_to: single-anchor spells only; self spells target the caster and shaped spells derive geometry from a chosen direction, so a per-cell field would describe a geometry they do not have
spell_reach_presentation.marker: attack range texture at the range-envelope tier
spell_reach_presentation.rule: a cell is inside the declared reach when the preview fails only on what it found there, never on range or the sight line
spell_reach_presentation.why: a spell with no legal target still has to answer how far it reaches
spell_reach_presentation.dead_zone: uses the unreachable texture at the unavailable tier, and never marks the caster's own cell
spell_reach_presentation.review: EditMode empty-reach, out-of-reach and dead-zone tests pass; steady-state rendered alpha read back 0.27 for the reach field; human aesthetic review pending

enemy_intent_destination.marker: an orange cell frame (neutral white frame texture, tinted) plus a centred orange diamond
enemy_intent_destination.tint: bright orange #FF8A1F on the frame; the diamond's orange is baked into its texture, which is drawn white
enemy_intent_destination.placeholder: Art/FormalTacticalOverlays32V2/enemy_intent_diamond is a 32x32 diamond drawn programmatically on the user's explicit instruction, which this contract normally forbids; replace it with a generated source (hard alpha, single square macro-pixel grid, 1px outline) before the asset becomes formal
enemy_intent_destination.rule: the neutral white frame is the only frame in the project that can be tinted: the move-range corner brackets are cyan (R≈0), so multiplying them by any warm tint renders muddy (the old 'pale grey') and they are identical in form to the player's own range. Both parts stay near-opaque (0.9 > the strongest player tier 0.72) so a destination inside the player's reachable cells still reads.

context_menu_preview.source: CombatSelectionController menu preview state driven by FormalBattlefieldView row hover
context_menu_preview.on_open: only the anchor cell is marked as focus; the committed action's range is not drawn
context_menu_preview.on_row_hover: previews that row's selectable range and effect cells at the anchor
context_menu_preview.rows_without_preview: actions that cannot preview a range (armed tactical items) keep the anchor marker only, because an item only becomes 技能1 once the quickbar arms it
context_menu_preview.hover_arbitration: the view owns which row owns the preview, because a pointer moving between rows can deliver the old row exit after the new row enter
context_menu_preview.review: EditMode anchor/row/restore transitions pass; live pointer flow and human aesthetic review pending

lamp_vine.sampling: partition original UV without changing texture/importer/color; integer display at 64/128 reference cells
lamp_vine.depth: fixed cell ground depth; after actors on same row, before nearer actors; no unit travel inherited
lamp_vine.lifecycle: presented tile controls visibility at existing hit time; hide on burn, reuse on restoration; raycast disabled

terrain_depth_presentation.ground_attachments: catalog marks explicitly; parent to owning cell after floor, before environment and objects; raised structures retain structure layer
terrain_depth_presentation.review: empty whole/split production renders identical; motion depth and burn/restore inspected; full dynamic/human review pending; no asset promotion

unit_pixel_input.ownership: opaque displayed body pixels resolve to owning gameplay cell; existing hover/left/right command handlers retained
unit_pixel_input.transparency: source alpha >=128 is hittable; transparent pixels pass to next rendered unit or grid
unit_pixel_input.coordinates: current RectTransform, UV including flip, event camera and parent viewport clipping
unit_pixel_input.cache: one bit per texel; one capture per distinct texture at binding; non-readable source uses temporary GPU readback without importer mutation; no readback in pointer events
unit_pixel_input.lifecycle: components created lazily on occupied cells; cache scoped to view; readback failure leaves grid input and logs once
invariants: existing command eligibility and double-click movement
art files GUID and importer unchanged
unit_pixel_input.review: four production Canvas resolution/zoom cases plus overlap and transparency checked in EditMode; continuous Play input and runtime profiling remain pending

occlusion_readability.source: only currently presented unit source Alpha boundaries covered by later drawn opaque units or terrain fronts
occlusion_readability.geometry: one native world pixel UI quads on hidden boundary texels only; no filled silhouette or replacement raster
occlusion_readability.color: friendly cyan; enemy sealed red; alpha 0.9
occlusion_readability.layer: above units and terrain fronts, below information; inherits viewport RectMask2D
